Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

soilhub 0.2.0

First release of the redesigned client: one library for every user of the Global Soil Data Hub API, with what each user may do decided by the rights of the account. It follows the API 0.6.0 (reads raw and revised, first layer, profile types, components, summaries, exports, catalog with provenance, citations and licences) and replaces the 0.1.x client.

Tested: R CMD check on Linux, macOS and Windows (R 4.1 and current, with and without sf); contract tests against the API’s OpenAPI and recorded responses of production; live acceptance on production with a read-only account (reads of the 7 datasets, exports in 4 formats, session expiry and recovery, a session of 4 hours of reads plus 90 minutes idle without a new sign-in).

Known limitation: the write functions (soil_register_variable(), soil_publish_values(), soil_publish_health(), soil_publish_source(), runs and jobs) are tested against a simulated API only; the live write acceptance with a publisher account is scheduled after this release (giulange/soilhub-r#14).

Changes in this release

  • Documentation and site (WP11): six vignettes written for users with basic R, one small step per chunk with what it does and what the result means for a soil scientist: getting started (soilhub), raw-vs-revised, first-layer, exports, and writing-data (with the right each step needs). Their examples are evaluated when the vignettes are built, without network or login, against a local replay of the responses recorded from the production API (tests/testthat/fixtures/recorded; internal replay_session(), also used by the contract suite), so the outputs shown are real; sign-in, writes and large exports are shown but not run. New help page ?soilhub-terms (feature, profile, component, horizon, observation, PRID, HONU, SUID, TCID, SCID, CLAF, source_support, first_layer_status, views, markings, rights). Every argument of the reference names the API field it fills (or says it is client-side); the session functions and the configuration and error topics have their @family. _pkgdown.yml lists the articles and every reference topic; README: install, first use, licences and soil_citations().

  • Exports (WP7): soil_export() submits a selection (the arguments of soil_observations(), plus format, content and layout, checked against soil_capabilities()$exports: Shapefile only with content = "features"), polls it, downloads the zip into the export directory (soilhub.export_dir) and unzips it; wait = FALSE returns the job id at once. soil_export_status(), soil_export_wait() (failed, cancelled, an unknown id and a timeout are soilhub_job_errors with reason), soil_export_download() (streamed, never overwriting unless asked; an expired export is a soilhub_not_found_error with reason = "expired") and soil_export_cancel() (needs soil:publish) work from the object or the job id alone. soil_export_read() reads the tables of every format back, typed from metadata.json exactly as the synchronous reads type them (wide, long, features; JSON text cells parsed back to list columns); CSV, TSV and GeoJSON need no package, GeoPackage and Shapefile need sf. too_large = "export" of soil_observations() and soil_features() exports a refused selection and returns the same shape, with soil_metadata(x)$via_export; soil_export_from_error() is its manual form. soil_columns(), soil_citations() and soil_revised_rules() work on a downloaded export. soil_values() and soil_health_scores() accept with_geometry = "sf".

  • Contract tests and fixture recording (WP10): tests/contract/ checks the client against the API’s OpenAPI document (committed snapshot tests/contract/openapi.json, API 0.6.0, or the live one): every path and method the client calls, every query parameter, JSON body field and form field it sends (name, type, enum value, required fields), the enums it offers (selection_values, choices of the exported functions such as layout), the response fields of its typing tables where the OpenAPI types them, and the API version range. The client requests are not listed by hand: soil_request() hands every request to the development option soilhub.exchange_hook, and the suite records them from the unit tests. Rscript tests/contract/run.R [live] runs it (not part of R CMD check); .github/workflows/contract.yml runs it weekly with a diff of the live openapi.json against the snapshot (tools/update_contract_snapshots.R --check), without secrets. tools/record_fixtures.R (run by the owner with a device login) records scrubbed responses of a curated set of read calls and tests/contract/capabilities.json; the suite replays them through the client and skips until they exist. tools/check_version.R checks MIN_API_VERSION / SUPPORTED_API_MAJOR against an OpenAPI document. New constant TESTED_API_VERSION (0.6.0, the info.version of the snapshot, kept in step by tools/update_contract_snapshots.R and checked by the contract suite): the “API is newer than this client was tested with” message of soil_connect() now compares with it instead of MIN_API_VERSION (still 0.5.0, the oldest server accepted), so API 0.6.x gives no message. Streamed downloads (the export zip) pass through the exchange hook too, so the contract suite sees GET /exports/{job_id}/download; tools/record_fixtures.R --with-export adds one small export round trip (off by default: an export is a job written under the user’s name).

  • Long observations, features and geometry (WP5): soil_observations(layout = "long") reads one row per observation, typed per column family (value double, value_raw the source value verbatim as a list column, release_id and value_count integer, lineage, source descriptors and method_facets lists, marking columns, revised_markings with hidden_values as a data frame); soil_metadata(x)$total_count is the exact count of the selection. A multi-value WoSIS cell, for which the API extracts no number, gets the mean of its values in value, as the wide layout does. soil_features() reads the features (points and (multi)polygons) with feature_key, components (data frames), profile_markings and retired_in_release, and the metadata feature_count, feature_count_by_dataset and mixed_geometry. with_geometry = "sf" returns an sf soil_table (EPSG:4326) for the wide and long layouts and the features; "text" gives WKT (wide) or GeoJSON (long, features) without any package. sf stays in Suggests: without it "sf" raises a soilhub_dependency_error before any request. soil_flags() and soil_markings() read long tables too.

  • Summaries and thematic reads (WP6): soil_summary() and soil_availability() take the selection of soil_observations() (validated the same way, sent as the same body without the layout fields) and check the same optional capabilities; soil_summary() returns a soil_summary with the counts by dataset (filled with the total when one dataset is selected), the variable semantics, the revised rules and a short print method, and works with soil_metadata(), soil_revised_rules() and soil_citations(). soil_availability() returns data frames by dataset (distinct totals), country, dataset and country, and variable (with the scoped variants). soil_consistency() sends its own request (no view, profile type or components) and returns the distinct totals with the calculation used. Thematic reads: soil_values() (typed value column, lineage on request), soil_values_summary(), soil_health_scores() (details on request; the arguments run_ids and statuses are the API fields product_run_ids and score_statuses), soil_health_summary(), soil_resolve_targets() (requests of 10,000 targets, reads targets of the response; strict = TRUE stops on missing or ambiguous targets) and soil_ttr_flags() (GET /sotwis/ttr-flags, paged, source columns verbatim). Geometry of values and scores as GeoJSON text with with_geometry = "text"; "sf" follows with the geometry module.

  • Wide observations (WP4): soil_observations() reads the canonical wide layout (one row per horizon) page by page, with the selection of every canonical read (datasets, variables, bbox, country, geometry, layer, view, profile_type, components, min_cumulative_percent) validated before any request; view = "raw" is sent explicitly. The result is a soil_table (a data frame keeping its metadata through [), typed by column family: fixed, first-layer, component, source attribute and marking columns, value_flags, retirement, revised markings, WKT geometry text (with_geometry = "text") and the variable groups <key>, _units, _method, _n. Multi-value WoSIS cells: <key> holds the mean of the listed values and <key>_values every original value (multi_value_rule = "mean"). Pages with different column sets are aligned. A refused selection raises soilhub_load_limit_error naming the soil_export() call of the same selection; a failure after some pages keeps them as a typed partial soil_table in e$partial. Result helpers: soil_metadata(), soil_warnings(), soil_columns(), soil_flags(), soil_markings(), soil_revised_rules(), soil_first_layer(), print and summary methods. too_large = "export" follows in a later work package.

  • Writes and jobs (WP8), gated by the rights of the session (checked locally when the token declares them, else decided by the API; a 403 is a soilhub_permission_error naming the right): soil_register_variable() (validate then register, capability variable_registration), soil_product(), soil_product_version(), soil_run_open(), soil_run_complete(), soil_run_fail(), soil_publish_values() and soil_publish_health() (local checks of every record, server validation, synchronous up to 10,000 records, else an NDJSON file uploaded with its SHA-256 checksum as a job, never retried; receipts reconciled with the records sent, soilhub_reconciliation_warning), soil_job(), soil_job_wait(), soil_job_cancel() and soil_refresh_countries(). A 409 is a soilhub_conflict_error that says what to do (the API has no GET for products, versions or runs); a job that fails or is cancelled is a soilhub_job_error with the rejected rows in e$errors.

  • Source ingest (WP9): soil_publish_source() builds a provider-neutral NDJSON bundle (features from an sf object or a spatial file – a WGS84 GeoJSON file is read without sf – then profiles, components, horizons and observations), checks before any request the manifest, source_record_id (present, unique per record type), parent references, observation declarations, the CRS (transformed to EPSG:4326) and the geometry types, uploads it with its manifest and SHA-256 checksum (never retried), validates, verifies the counts staged by the API against the records sent (a difference stops before promotion), promotes and reconciles the published counts; auto_promote = TRUE lets the server’s ingest worker validate and promote while the client waits; keep_file = TRUE keeps the bundle. Unmapped property codes are a soilhub_unmapped_properties_warning. soil_source_validate() and soil_source_promote() run the two server steps separately.

  • A 403 on a session whose token does not declare its rights no longer reports the rights as FALSE.

  • Discovery and version check (WP3): after the login soil_connect() reads /capabilities and checks the API version (0.5.0 or later, major 0) and the required capabilities; an incompatible server stops with soilhub_capability_error (the signed-out session in e$session), a newer minor version prints a message. Optional capabilities are checked by the functions that need them (FALSE is an error, not advertised a warning). New: soil_capabilities(), soil_api_info(), soil_datasets() and soil_dataset() (catalog with the provenance of the release, source assets and notes), soil_citations() and soil_licences() (provider texts verbatim, per source dataset from the notes when no dataset-level text exists), soil_formats(), soil_variables(), soil_variable_mappings(), soil_countries(), soil_country(), soil_code_lists(), soil_code_list(), soil_ttr_flag_legend(). Every result is a typed data frame; nested objects are list columns of data frames; fields unknown to the client are kept as list columns with a soilhub_contract_warning.

  • Query strings no longer pad repeated character values to a common width.

  • Sessions (WP2): soil_connect() signs in with the Keycloak device login (PKCE, human users only, tokens in memory only), soil_login(), soil_logout(), the default session soil_session() and soil_whoami() (user, rights read from the token, advertised limits, session lifetime). The access token is renewed automatically before it expires (margin soilhub.refresh_margin, default 60 s) and once after an HTTP 401, storing the rotated refresh token; a session Keycloak no longer renews fails with soilhub_auth_error(reason = "session_expired") once the current access token has expired (a warning announces it). Rights are checked locally only when the token declares them for the API audience. The print method of a session never shows a token. A 403 names the right the request needs.

  • HTTP layer, errors and paging (WP1): one internal request function with client request ids (X-Request-ID), retries on transport failures and HTTP 429/502/503/504 honouring Retry-After (capped at 10 s), connect timeout 10 s and total timeout 300 s; the condition classes of ?soilhub-errors (including soilhub_load_limit_error with the equivalent soil_export() call); an offset page collector with partial results on failure; the configuration precedence and verbosity levels of ?soilhub-config.

  • Package skeleton of the 0.2.0 redesign: DESCRIPTION, tests with a fake-API helper, CI matrix and pkgdown configuration. No user-facing functions yet. The 0.1.x client documented in docs/legacy/TUTORIAL-0.1.md is superseded.
